hints: Remember what ethanolic NaOH does to a halogenoalkane, think elimination to form an alkene rather than substitution.
For elimination to happen you need a hydrogen on the carbon next door to the C-Br carbon, so check the carbon adjacent to Br in each structure.
Look for the structure where the neighbour carbon has only methyl groups and no H at all, as that one cannot lose HBr to make a double bond.
walkthrough:
**Recall the reaction condition**

Great start, let's remember the chemistry. Ethanolic NaOH causes dehydrohalogenation, which is elimination of HBr to form an alkene.

General elimination:
$$\text{R-CH}_2\text{-CHBr-R'} \xrightarrow[\text{heat}]{\text{ethanolic NaOH}} \text{R-CH=CH-R'} + \text{HBr}$$

**Spot the requirement for elimination**

To make the C=C double bond, you must remove Br from one carbon and H from the adjacent (beta) carbon. If there is no H on the adjacent carbon, elimination is impossible.

**Examine 1-bromo-2,2-dimethylpropane**

Now draw it out in your head. The structure is $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-CH}_2\text{Br}$.

The $\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ carbon is joined to a central C that is bonded to three $\text{CH}_3$ groups and has zero hydrogens. With no beta-hydrogen, no alkene can form, so this fits the observation.

options.A: 1-bromo-2-methylbutane is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$. The adjacent C2 has one H, so HBr can be eliminated to give an alkene such as 3-methylbut-1-ene. It would form an alkene, so it is not the answer.
options.B: 2-bromo-2-methylbutane is $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CBrCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. This is a tertiary bromoalkane with plenty of H atoms on the neighbouring carbons, so it eliminates very readily to give mainly 2-methylbut-2-ene. It would form an alkene.
options.C: 3-bromopentane is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHBrCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Both adjacent carbons (C2 and C4) have two H atoms each, so elimination easily gives pent-2-ene. It would form an alkene.
options.D: 1-bromo-2,2-dimethylpropane is $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-CH}_2\text{Br}$. The C-Br carbon is attached to a quaternary carbon with no hydrogens, so there is no beta-hydrogen to remove. Elimination to form an alkene is impossible, matching the observation perfectly.
